title: Other Tables
tagline: Six passes out of one batch. Bureau's going to love that number and hate what it means.

intro.speaker: Narrator
intro.text: The same admin room. Tao's feed closed out long ago. Other batch feeds still trickle in across the bank of monitors — one shows a clearing, wrapped up and quiet. No fire. No wreckage. Nothing dramatic to report.

intro.speaker: Admin
intro.text: That one's done too. Nothing like the fireworks Tao gave us.

intro.speaker: Admin
intro.text: Not every examiner needs to level a forest to make a point.

The door opens. Chiara walks in unhurried, flipping a card between two fingers — and tucks it away the instant she clears the doorway, like she wasn't doing anything and didn't want anyone confirming it. She drops into a chair, boots up on the console edge.

intro.speaker: Admin
intro.text: Done already? Heard you had a full batch — thought yours might run long.

intro.speaker: Chiara
intro.text: Ran long enough. Three pairs worth telling you about, actually.

intro.speaker: Admin
intro.text: Go on then. We've got a minute before Phase 2 kicks off.

outro.speaker: Narrator
outro.text: No ceremony. No forced exposition. Just someone who enjoys a good story telling it to two people who enjoy hearing them.

intro.text: Batra takes a hit early — and smiles. Every exchange after that he's faster, heavier, hungrier. Chiara drops a dice-construct on him expecting it to slow him down. Instead it visibly feeds him. Pain answering the oldest law of Toll: the more it costs him, the more he burns.

Gabrist has been quiet the whole time. Watching. Timing. The moment Chiara commits to a real technique he flicks two fingers and it unravels mid-formation — but he staggers a half-step doing it, breath short, like the cancel cost him something real. He can afford that once. Maybe twice. Both of them know it.

outro.speaker: Narrator
outro.text: It closes with Batra still trying to close distance while Gabrist quietly pulls him back a step — reading the fight better than Batra reads it himself.

outro.speaker: Chiara
outro.text: The big one hits harder the longer it goes — didn't expect that. The quiet one only gets one good trick out of him before he's running on fumes. Between them, almost enough.

intro.text: Mustafa plants and holds — an earthen wall that doesn't chip, doesn't crack, just is. He isn't trying to hurt her. He isn't trying to do anything except remain.
Siddiq stays half a step behind, vines threading briefly over Mustafa's forearm to seal a graze shut without either of them breaking formation. Neither steps forward to strike.
Chiara throws everything she has — full gambles, real technique, calculated risk — and there is nothing on the other end to win against. No opening. No damage that matters. No offense to punish.

outro.speaker: Narrator
outro.text: Eventually she just stops. Lowers her hand.

outro.speaker: Chiara
outro.text: Two shields and a stalemate isn't a hand I can play.
She passes them looking almost betrayed by how little there was to bet on.

intro.text: Yalina never stops talking — needling, mocking, dragging every ounce of Chiara's attention onto herself, absorbing hits she could have dodged just to keep the target where she wants it.
Sara is barely there half the time. Gone before the strike lands, already circling — a graze here, a cut there, a slow bleed nobody notices building.
Chiara, baited and irritated, finally overcommits on Yalina with something real. It is exactly the opening Yalina wanted.

outro.speaker: Narrator
outro.text: She eats the hit clean, doesn't flinch, and answers with everything she has in one committed strike while Chiara is still resetting. It lands.
Chiara laughs out loud — the first genuine sound she's made all afternoon. Sara, still circling at the edge of frame, hasn't taken a clean hit once.

outro.speaker: Chiara
outro.text: Mouth draws the fire. Legs never stop moving. And somewhere in between, one hit that actually mattered.

outro.speaker: Chiara
outro.text: Six passes out of one batch. Bureau's going to love that number and hate what it means.

outro.speaker: Admin
outro.text: Speaking of — Phase 2's about to start. You clocked out already, you know. Don't have to stick around.

outro.speaker: Chiara
outro.text: Just want to see what happens next.
